headline.detector: Every scored dimension identical to baseline on all four states. Recall 1.0000 and code accuracy perfect everywhere (AZ 4/4, CA 25/25, CO 7/7, TX 8/8). The ONLY difference in the whole re-record is AZ n_detected 66 -> 67, and AZ in-scope precision is unchanged at 0.4167, so the extra element fell outside the annotated domains and is not scored.
headline.parser: Byte-identical to baseline on every state and field. AZ 17/18 fully correct (field accuracy 0.9969), CA 21/21, CO 9/9, TX 8/8, no id collisions anywhere.
headline.interpretation: Seven code-version moves changed nothing on the four states used to tune the system. That is what lets task2_20260826's held-out gain (NV code accuracy 44/46 -> 46/46) be read as generalization rather than a global shift.

caveats: THE AZ DUPLICATE-DETECTION DROP DOES NOT APPEAR IN THIS ARM. A batched-path observation on pipeline run 043 showed AZ detection falling 77 -> 65, entirely listing-page duplicate sub_strands, prompting a prediction that AZ raw precision would rise and invert the caution at tasking/arxiv_paper.md line 127. On the direct path AZ went 66 -> 67 and in-scope precision did not move. The line-127 caution stands unmodified for the eval numbers; the batched-path observation is an open question about production output, not about this table.

GUARDRAIL 8 UNCHANGED. Raw precision on the golden four (AZ 0.4167, CA 0.2049, CO 0.1667, TX 0.3200) measures annotation coverage, not detector quality — these goldens are 5-25 element spot checks against 12-122 in-scope detections.
